_meta.description: Opening-specific plans, ideas, and typical themes for Game Decryption

queens_indian.name: Queen's Indian Defense
queens_indian.white_plan: Control the center with d4+c4, develop pieces actively, often fianchetto kingside with g3+Bg2
queens_indian.black_plan: Fianchetto bishop to b7 to pressure e4 and the long diagonal, flexible center with d6 or d5

typical_ideas.b6: Preparing to fianchetto the bishop to b7, controlling the long diagonal
typical_ideas.Bb7: Completing the fianchetto, the bishop now pressures e4 and the long diagonal toward g2
typical_ideas.d6: Supporting e5 if needed, keeping options open
typical_ideas.c5: Attacking White's d4 pawn, fighting for central space
typical_ideas.Bb4+: Pinning the knight, or forcing White to make a decision
typical_ideas.g3: Preparing the fianchetto, mirrors Black's setup
typical_ideas.Bg2: Completing White's fianchetto, controlling the long diagonal
typical_ideas.a3: Preventing Bb4 check or preparing b4 expansion

common_mistakes.early_e5: e5 too early can leave the d5 square weak
common_mistakes.passive_bishop: Don't leave the bishop on c8 too long - it belongs on b7

phase_focus.opening: Complete fianchetto setup, castle, connect rooks
phase_focus.middlegame: Use the bishop on b7 to pressure White's center, look for d5 or c5 breaks

london_system.name: London System
london_system.white_plan: Solid pawn structure d4+e3, bishop to f4 before e3, develop harmoniously
london_system.black_plan: Challenge the bishop with Nh5 or c5, don't let White get a comfortable position

typical_ideas.Bf4: The signature London move - develop bishop BEFORE playing e3
typical_ideas.e3: Solidifying the center, but must be played AFTER Bf4
typical_ideas.c3: Supporting d4, preparing Nbd2 or Qb3
typical_ideas.Nbd2: Flexible - can go to f3, e4, or b3
typical_ideas.Nh5: Kicking the London bishop, forcing Bg3 or Be5
typical_ideas.Qb6: Attacking b2 and pressuring the queenside

common_mistakes.e3_before_bf4: Playing e3 before Bf4 locks the bishop inside - major London sin!
common_mistakes.passive_play: Don't just develop - have a plan to create pressure

phase_focus.opening: Bf4 before e3! Then solid development and castle
phase_focus.middlegame: Look for kingside attack with pieces or queenside pressure

sicilian_najdorf.name: Sicilian Najdorf
sicilian_najdorf.white_plan: Use the central space advantage, launch kingside attack or play f3+Be3 setup
sicilian_najdorf.black_plan: Use a6 to prepare b5 expansion, counterplay on queenside while White attacks kingside

typical_ideas.a6: The Najdorf move - prevents Bb5, prepares b5 expansion
typical_ideas.e5: Controlling d4 and f4, cramping Black but weakening d5
typical_ideas.Be3: Developing and preparing to castle queenside
typical_ideas.Bb7: After b5, the bishop becomes active
typical_ideas.Nbd7: Flexible development, can go to c5, b6, or e5

common_mistakes.premature_e5: Playing e5 without preparation can be met with d5!
common_mistakes.forgetting_development: Don't push pawns without developing pieces

phase_focus.opening: Complete development, prepare for sharp middlegame
phase_focus.middlegame: Black attacks queenside (b5-b4), White attacks kingside (g4-h4 or f4-f5)

italian_game.name: Italian Game
italian_game.white_plan: Target f7 weakness, develop quickly, castle and attack
italian_game.black_plan: Solid development with Bc5 or Nf6, challenge e4 with d6 or d5

typical_ideas.Bc4: Targeting f7, the weakest point in Black's position
typical_ideas.d3: The Giuoco Pianissimo - slow but solid
typical_ideas.c3: Preparing d4 to challenge the center
typical_ideas.d6: Supporting e5, keeping the position solid
typical_ideas.d5: The main break - only play when ready!

common_mistakes.premature_d5: d5 too early loses the center after exd5
common_mistakes.forgetting_castling: Don't delay castling - the center can open quickly

phase_focus.opening: Develop pieces toward the center, castle kingside
phase_focus.middlegame: Look for d4 break (White) or d5 break (Black)

caro_kann.name: Caro-Kann Defense
caro_kann.white_plan: Occupy the center with d4, try to limit Black's light-squared bishop
caro_kann.black_plan: Solid pawn structure, develop bishop outside the pawn chain before e6

typical_ideas.c6: Preparing d5 to challenge e4 immediately
typical_ideas.d5: The point of c6 - challenging the center
typical_ideas.Bf5: Getting the bishop out BEFORE playing e6
typical_ideas.e6: Solid but locks the bishop - play Bf5 first!
typical_ideas.Bd3: White often trades this bishop for Black's good Bf5

common_mistakes.e6_before_bf5: Playing e6 before Bf5 locks the bishop inside - bad!
common_mistakes.passive_play: Don't be too solid - look for counterplay

phase_focus.opening: Get Bf5 out before e6! Solid development.
phase_focus.middlegame: Use the solid structure to outplay opponent in the long term

french_defense.name: French Defense
french_defense.white_plan: Use space advantage, attack the kingside, restrict Black's light bishop
french_defense.black_plan: Attack the pawn chain with c5 and f6, activate the bad bishop

typical_ideas.e6: Solid, preparing d5, but locks in the light bishop
typical_ideas.c5: THE key break - attacking the base of White's pawn chain
typical_ideas.f6: Secondary break - attacking e5, but weakens the king
typical_ideas.Bd7: Often necessary to connect rooks, but passive
typical_ideas.b6+Bb7: Fianchetto can activate the bad bishop
typical_ideas.e5: White's space-gaining move, but creates a target
typical_ideas.f4: White reinforces e5 and prepares kingside attack

common_mistakes.forgetting_c5: c5 is essential - without it Black suffocates
common_mistakes.bad_bishop: Don't ignore the light bishop problem - find ways to activate it

phase_focus.opening: Play c5 early! It's the key to counterplay.
phase_focus.middlegame: Attack the pawn chain, try to trade the bad bishop

kings_indian.name: King's Indian Defense
kings_indian.white_plan: Control center, expand on queenside with c5, play in the center
kings_indian.black_plan: Fianchetto kingside, prepare f5 or e5 breaks, launch kingside attack

typical_ideas.g6+Bg7: The fianchetto setup - the bishop becomes a monster on the diagonal
typical_ideas.e5: THE main break - creates closed center, then f5-f4 attack
typical_ideas.d5: White closes the center - now it's a race: queenside vs kingside
typical_ideas.b4: White gains space on the queenside

common_mistakes.passive_play: KID is about attack - don't play passively!
common_mistakes.wrong_timing: e5 and f5 need proper timing - don't rush

phase_focus.middlegame: After d5, race begins - Black attacks kingside with f5-f4, White attacks queenside

ruy_lopez.name: Ruy Lopez (Spanish Game)
ruy_lopez.white_plan: Pressure the e5 pawn through the knight on c6, slow maneuvering game
ruy_lopez.black_plan: Solid defense, prepare d5 break, counterplay with a5/b5

typical_ideas.Bb5: Putting pressure on Nc6 which defends e5
typical_ideas.a6: The Morphy Defense - kicking the bishop, preparing b5
typical_ideas.b5: Expanding on queenside, giving the bishop a retreat square
typical_ideas.Bb3: Safe square for the bishop, still eyes f7

common_mistakes.losing_e5: Don't lose the e5 pawn without compensation
common_mistakes.passive_defense: Black must find counterplay, not just defend

phase_focus.opening: Solid development, don't panic about the bishop on b5
phase_focus.middlegame: White slowly builds pressure, Black looks for d5 break

default.name: General Opening
default.white_plan: Control the center, develop pieces, castle for king safety
default.black_plan: Contest the center, develop pieces actively, ensure king safety

typical_ideas.e4: Classic center pawn, controls d5 and f5, opens diagonals for queen and bishop
typical_ideas.d4: Classic center pawn, controls c5 and e5, opens diagonal for queen-bishop
typical_ideas.Nf3: Developing toward center, controlling e5 and d4
typical_ideas.Nc3: Developing toward center, supporting e4 or d5
typical_ideas.O-O: King safety - essential in most openings
typical_ideas.castling: Get your king safe and connect your rooks

phase_focus.opening: 1) Control center, 2) Develop pieces, 3) Castle, 4) Connect rooks
phase_focus.middlegame: Create a plan based on the pawn structure
phase_focus.endgame: Activate your king, create passed pawns
